fatal_errors: Misidentifies characterization by TEM/SEM as the fabrication method; the relevant method is liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu.
Omits the selective dissolution/exchange of Ti-rich interdendritic regions and retention of W/Ta/V-rich RHEA ligaments.
Omits the essential 1200 °C, 96 h vacuum-sealed reaction condition.
Does not reconstruct the bicontinuous, directionally aligned RHEA–Cu architecture or the W-rich passivating interlayer.
Provides no evidence that in-situ microscopy can overcome the positive heat of mixing or produce a large-scale stable composite.
The proposed falsification test confounds observation with intervention: characterization itself is not expected to improve material properties.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad relevance of RHEAs, high-temperature stability, and microscopy, but it does not answer which processing method forms the RHEA–Cu composite or why it is stable. The target uses liquid-metal dealloying of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu: Ti-rich channels preferentially exchange with Cu, continuous refractory-rich ligaments remain, and a W-rich interfacial layer passivates the interface and arrests further reaction. The cited evidence supports only generic RHEA high-temperature properties and does not support in-situ TEM/SEM as a scalable reaction or stabilization method. Its proposed experiment could document microstructure but cannot causally test the claimed processing benefit.
